frequency_question: How often do proposed countercyclical capital buffer increases above the baseline (0%) successfully pass through regulatory friction to official adoption within a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes formal proposals or active policy discussions by major jurisdictions (US, UK, Eurozone) to raise the CCyB above 0% during post-Basel III implementation periods. Excludes routine maintenance or decreases.

coverage_note: 6 major regulatory observation sets across key jurisdictions; captures the friction barrier where inaction (keeping at 0%) is the default state.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market central banks where institutional friction operates differently.
skeleton: Regulatory jurisdictions with institutional frameworks for CCyB; split between active non-zero deployments and inert baseline maintenance under structural friction.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 6 major institutional review instances where structural friction regarding procyclicality was actively debated.
validity_reason: Basel III structural capital frameworks and regulatory inertia dynamics remain stable across this decade.
